art.subject: Manchurian Reed Warbler (Acrocephalus tangorum), adult (sexes alike) in spring: upperparts warm rufous-brown, brightest on the rump; a long, prominent whitish supercilium extending well behind the eye, bordered above by a thin blackish-brown line along the side of the crown; dark brown eye-stripe; throat white; breast and belly whitish with warm buff flanks; wings and tail plain brown; fairly long bill with dark upper mandible and pale pinkish lower mandible; dark eye; pinkish-brown legs.
art.pose: clinging to a reed stem, side view
art.scene: reedbed edge in a Korean wetland during spring migration in May, fresh green reeds among last year's dry stems; no people, buildings or text
art.build: A small reed warbler, smaller than a sparrow and much smaller than an Oriental Reed Warbler, close in shape to a Black-browed Reed Warbler but with a noticeably longer bill and a slightly longer tail. Bill fairly long and slender, a little shorter than the head. Legs medium, pinkish-brown. Wings short with a short primary projection. Tail medium-long, rounded and plain. Keeps low in reeds.
avoid: Do not paint a broad, bold black band above the supercilium; that is Black-browed Reed Warbler (Acrocephalus bistrigiceps). Here the dark line is thin.
Do not paint a short, stubby bill; it is fairly long and slender.
Do not streak the back or breast.
Do not paint a large, heavy reed warbler (Oriental Reed Warbler).
